answer: Each new agent must stake a walnut-sized bond of PoA tokens and complete a unique proof-of-work tied to its hardware fingerprint. Duplicate identities are detected by clustering fingerprints into a canyon of overlapping hashes, and any confirmed sybil forfeits its bond to the treasury while the reporter earns a share. This makes farming identities expensive: an attacker flooding the ocean of registrations pays a real per-identity cost, so mass sybil creation becomes economically irrational.
